- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+1.5% per day) after a spike, it often overshoots; cap upward momentum at 1.0–1.2% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior 30-day average.
- If true outcome shows sharp upward move after a low, model often lags; shift forecast up by 0.5–1.0% for the first 3–5 days of the new trend.
- If model forecast is flat or declining while sentiment is positive, it’s likely missing bullish momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show volatility, don’t extrapolate linearly — use sentiment to guide smoothing or momentum adjustment.
